title_original: ‘Filipiñana’ breakout star Jorrybell Agoto dies at 32
excerpt_original: The Sundance award-winning film is the Philippines’ submission to the Oscars.

blocks.text: Jorrybell Agoto, the star of Philippines Oscar submission Filipiñana , has died aged 32.
Her family announced that the actress died on Tuesday (November 17) following a battle with lymphoma. Her wake will be held from November 21-28, with a funeral scheduled on November 29.

Agoto was best known as the lead actress of Filipiñana , in which she starred as a 17-year-old tee girl at a pristine resort on the outskirts of Manila where she discovers sinister revelations about its elite members and her own past.

The film received its world premiere at Sundance in January, where it won the World Cinema Dramatic special jury prize for creative vision, and went on to screen at festivals including the Berlinale and Pingyao, where filmmaker Rafael Manuel won best director for the feature.
It is also generating strong buzz of landing a shortlist position in the international feature film category of the upcoming Academy Awards.

“The tragedy of this loss cannot be put into words,” said Filipiñana director Manuel. “The world has just lost one of its brightest stars. We have just lost a great friend. But our thoughts and prayers go out especially to Jorrybell’s family who have just lost a loving ate [Filipino word for older sister] and a devoted daughter.”
Agoto previously worked with Manual on 2020 short Filipiñana – only her second ever on-screen role – which won the Silver Bear jury prize at the Berlinale and inspired the feature.

Further credits include Lawrence Fajardo’s Silenced Nights , which played at Toronto in September; Jun Robles Lana’s Sisa , which premiered at Tallinn Black Nights in 2025; Kevin Mayuga’s When This Is All Over in 2023; and Gian Arre’s Tether, also in 2023.

She also appeared in shorts such as Cross My Heart Hope To Die , which was selected for Venice Horizons in 2023; and The Slums , her debut film, a winner at the Busan International Kids and Youth Film Festival in 2019.
Agoto was a graduate of AB Theatre Arts in the Philippines.

Filipiñana is opening in the UK and Ireland this weekend through BFI Distribution. It received a US release in August. Kino Lorber, which has the film’s North American rights, has been organising a series of special screenings as part of its Oscar campaign, of which one post-screening Q&A was moderated by Oscar-winning Anora director Sean Baker.
